newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austrian shares end up, eye 1,200 points.
newsitem.headline: Austrian shares end up, eye 1,200 points.

text.p: Austrian shares ended a seesaw session in positive territory on Thursday and traders said the ATX index could advance above the key psychological 1,200-point level in the near term, given a positive international lead.
The ATX index of 21 blue chip shares closed up 0.91 points, or 0.08 percent, at 1,187.92. Earlier it touched a low of 1,180.64.
"If the international environment is right we will break 1,190 points and then the 1,200-point level will go," a market participant said.
Demand centred on cylical stocks like fireproof materials manufacturer Radex-Heraklith and steelmaker VA Stahl.
Vienna airport company Flughafen Wien and oil group OMV were also sought.
Radex continued to reap the benefits of positive 1996 earnings data released on Wednesday. Its shares added on four schillings to finish at 400 in unusually brisk trade.
OMV, which presented record 1996 pre-tax earnings on Wednesday, recovered from Wednesday's bout of profit taking to end 7.1 schillings up at 1,330.

Flughafen was the day's biggest gainer and among the most actively traded shares, rising 12 schillings, or 2.19 percent, to 560. VA Stahl topped turnover with 87,491 contracts and closed 4.6 schillings higher at 430.5.

Paper maker Leykam was the leading decliner, down 6.5 schillings, or 2.23 pct, at 284.5 schillings. Last month its Dutch parent announced plans to cut around 500 jobs in Austria as part of a savings package.
The broad-based Vienna Bourse index closed 0.94 points up at 443.68. -- Vienna Newsroom, 43-1-53112-258
